activities.anchor: can never be sold for tonight
activities.caption: true or false — the perishable product
activities.name: gtmPerishJudge

statements.s: Tourism can be stored and sold later when demand picks up
statements.why: It cannot be stored, only sold now or lost — economists call it a perishable product.

statements.s: Perishability explains last-minute bargains and shoulder-season discounts
statements.why: A seat that would otherwise expire is sold at almost any price — any price above the small extra cost beats an empty seat.

statements.s: The 2020 pandemic was merely a bad year, and the unsold stock was recovered later
statements.why: It was a write-off of a quarter of the world's tourism stock — the product is perishable, though the desire is durable.

statements.s: An aircraft costs nearly the same to fly whether seat 24F is empty or occupied
statements.why: The extra passenger adds only a little fuel and a cup of coffee — the arithmetic of a perishable product, not desperation.

activities.anchor: of the trip changes the product being bought
activities.caption: pair each purpose with what it buys
activities.name: gtmPurposeMatch

config.prompt: One tourist, a different product for each — pair the purpose with its purchase:

pairs.right: meetings, incentives, conferences, exhibitions — rooms midweek, halls and reliable Wi-Fi
book late, stay long, spend little on hotels but much in shops
birders, divers, pilgrims, festival-goers — far out of season for one experience no other place offers

config.why: The business guest typically spends more per day than a leisure guest — each category is a point of view, not just a label.

activities.anchor: domestic trips at roughly three in four
activities.caption: call the share — the trips that never cross a border
activities.name: gtmDomesticEstimate

config.prompt: What share of all tourism trips worldwide are domestic?
config.why: Roughly three in four — most tourism never crosses a border, and business and VFR travel together rival leisure in value.
config.context: The sales rep asleep in the airport hotel is as much a tourist, statistically, as the snorkeller.

activities.anchor: arrivals meaning trips into a destination, not distinct people
activities.caption: fill the two headline numbers
activities.name: gtmScaleCloze

config.text: In 2019 the world recorded about %%0%% international tourist arrivals — and before the pandemic, travel and tourism supported roughly %%1%% of the planet's jobs.
config.hint: First blank: a count with a unit. Second blank: a simple fraction of jobs.

activities.anchor: The families interact, and real demand is always several
activities.caption: file each driver under its family
activities.name: gtmDriversBuckets

config.prompt: Six families of demand factors — file each driver:

items.label: rising wages and newly common paid vacations
jets, jumbos, budget fares and online booking
artificial wave pools that put surf breaks inland
Europe's free-movement rules turning a continent into one market
borders closing or reopening move the line instantly

config.why: The package holiday needed cheap jets and rising wages and paid annual leave; Spain's 1960s boom combined imported technology, government funding and a rising tide of northern-European holidaymakers.

activities.anchor: The surfing world is a miniature of the whole industry
activities.caption: find the faulty line — the sustainability shift
activities.name: gtmSurfSpot

config.prompt: One line of this summary is wrong — click it:
lines: As warm-water breaks grow crowded, enthusiasts seek out cold-water coastlines once considered unappealing.
Wave-park technology creates inland destinations that did not exist.
Eco-friendly board materials answer changed customer attitudes.
Media influence, wider availability of sustainable products and government policy all shift demand.
The sustainable shift stops at niche markets and never touches them.
config.correction: The shift reaches deep into niche markets — the surfing world is a miniature of the whole industry.
config.why: Demand, not just supply, keeps redrawing the map of where tourism happens — sustainable tourism is syllabus 2.1b for a reason.

activities.anchor: Two real destinations show the checklist working
activities.caption: manage the appeal — make the calls
activities.name: gtmManageBranch

config.root: You manage a city of 1.6 million that receives over 30 million visitors in some years. Resident protests are growing. What do you do?

start.text: The features that succeeded became the management problem that followed.

choices.label: Cap licensed tourist beds and restrict cruise terminals
choices.feedback: Barcelona's response — managing the appeal rather than merely enjoying it.

choices.label: Court more cruise passengers ashore for a few hours
choices.feedback: Volume, not value: day-trippers who spend only on coffee.

choices.label: Curate for exclusivity: one hub, expensive and protective
choices.feedback: The Maldives's play — flights to one hub island, then seaplanes and boats, keeping numbers manageable per island.

cap.text: The cap is the management problem being answered: culture, architecture and a Mediterranean climate with superb accessibility drew the crowds; the city government now limits the beds and the cruise terminals.

volume.text: Millions received, comparatively little earned — volume and value are different axes, and destination managers choose which to grow.

value.text: Some 1,200 coral islands and year-round warmth, sold through a deliberately curated accessibility — expensive, exclusive, and protective by design.

config.why: A destination is never simply 'good' — it is good for someone; and the two strategies build very different resorts.

activities.caption: drag the divider — appeal before and after the feed
activities.name: gtmAppealCompare

config.prompt: The relationship between feature and tourist type, before and after — drag the divider:

before.label: The unnoticed feature
before.text: A culture nobody has noticed, a coastline considered unappealing — invisible to the market.

after.label: The viral boom
after.text: A film or a feed makes it visible — and visibility re-ranks the checklist within a decade.

config.why: Appeal is a relationship between a feature and a tourist type at a moment in time, and both sides move — analyse a destination by linking a named feature to a named tourist type, then to how the feature is being managed.
